name: Sore Loser
why: A catch-up sting aimed at the contest leader, who sees it coming and can shrug off 3 followers.

name: Walk-In
why: A free blind draw is a little surprise for the owner, and every rival gets a red gift.

name: Loyalists
why: Quiet protection; no moment when played, nobody is hurt.

name: Trendsetters
why: Small shop nudge on each recruit; fine, rarely a highlight.

name: Spoilsport
why: The player who earned a contest (up to +10 in round III) gets it wiped at round end with no answer; feels robbed.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Same-cost swap each round; the victim keeps equal value, so it stings mildly but is fair.

name: Lie Low
why: Small steal plus a shield; fine.

name: Heist
why: Taking 3 followers is a clean, modest hit; fine on both sides.

name: Echo
why: Copying the move just made is a fun read-the-table moment for the owner.

name: Shoplifter
why: A drip of 1 stolen resource per recruit; fine, barely felt.

name: Panel
why: A swap with a rival on recruit; the rival gets a member back, so it is fine but not a highlight.

name: Demote
why: You trade down and the rival gets the better member; fine.

name: Doormen
why: Once a round you pick a rival's member to bury and hand them a worse one; they lose a member before round III with no answer.

name: Agents
why: Quiet passive block on copying; fine.

name: Potluck
why: Rivals pick what they give and come out ahead in silver; a gift that feels good on both sides.

name: Mob
why: A big round-end payoff for leading red is a satisfying moment, and rivals can race red to block it.

name: Philanthropist
why: Gifting silver for followers is a gift to rivals and a pleasant moment for the owner.

name: Sample
why: Borrowing a rival's best On Recruit while they keep it is a clever, fun moment with no victim.

name: Old Maid
why: No fun to recruit, and when a rival hands it to you you lose 5 followers with no answer.

name: Raiders
why: Once-a-game follower steal with 2 white paid back; fine.

name: Crunch Time
why: Two extra turns in a row is a strong, fun tempo moment.

name: Debt Collectors
why: A once-a-game 2-silver tax on everyone; fine, mild sting.

name: Grifter
why: Scaled steal on recruit; fine.

name: Farewell
why: Cashing a member into followers is a fine tradeoff, not a big moment.

name: Bury
why: Hate-burying a shop member is fine; small payoff.

name: High Society
why: Passive followers off rivals' silver moves; fine.

name: Spree
why: Recruiting three times in round III is a big, fun turn.

name: Fan Club
why: Copying the leader's action is a fun catch-up moment with no victim.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion in the last round is a satisfying power moment.

name: Tribute Band
why: Doing every action a rival took this round is a huge, memorable turn; the rival loses nothing.

name: Window Shopper
why: Burying two shop cards for resources is fine, not a highlight.

name: Early Birds
why: Quiet immunity to skips; fine.

name: Impersonator
why: Choosing a rival's ability to wear each round is a fun puzzle, and they keep theirs.

name: Window Dressers
why: A one-time shop shuffle; fine.

name: Largesse
why: A big gift to rivals that pays the owner in followers; pleasant for everyone.

name: Party Crasher
why: Jumping onto a taken space is a fun surprise; the rival keeps their own gain.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reading where rivals sit for resources is fine, small.

name: Poach
why: Taking any rival's member in round III is a big owner moment; it is on the open center space, so it can be seen coming.

name: Martyrs
why: Pays you when someone takes it; a satisfying counter moment.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two members for one buy is a pleasing moment.

name: Help Yourself
why: A spread steal of a few resources; fine on both sides.

name: Meddler
why: Changing one resource per rival is a small nuisance; fine.

name: Line Cutters
why: Always going first is a quiet edge; fine.

name: Creditor
why: A rival you pick trades 2 followers for 3 silver each round; compensated, so fine rather than robbed.

name: Bouncers
why: Skips only delay rivals' turns; fine.

name: Customs Officer
why: Small reaction payout; fine.

name: Savings
why: Resources plus a shop nudge; fine.

name: Cutpurse
why: 1 resource from the richest each round; barely felt.

name: Double Agent
why: You take any member from a rival and hand them a 1-follower card; losing a good member before round III feels robbed.

name: Guest of Honor
why: Handing a rival a cheap member is a gift and pays the owner 4 followers.

name: Debutantes
why: Doubling your silver is a big moment and rivals get silver too.

name: Night Watch
why: Pays off rivals' Goes Last moves; fine.

name: Accomplice
why: A cheap 3-resource steal; fine.

name: Scavenger
why: Grabbing a buried card is occasional and fine.

name: Last Call
why: Followers for held minions and going last; fine tradeoff.

name: Toast
why: A big silver gain that gifts every rival too.

name: Initiation
why: A free member up to 8 in round III is a satisfying payoff.

name: Godparent
why: Giving a rival a member for followers is mostly a gift; fun timing decision.

name: Deprogrammers
why: A small 1-follower pile-on when you take a member; fine.

name: Right Away
why: Back-to-back turns for a little purple; fine.

name: Hostesses
why: Silver gifts every round that pay you followers; pleasant for all.

name: Fence
why: Pays you when robbed; fine.

name: Con Men
why: A 5-resource steal on recruit spread among rivals; fine.

name: Extortionist
why: Steals from the richest each round; the leader in resources can see it and shrugs it off.

name: Closer
why: A bonus for placing last; fine.

name: Hot Streak
why: Lining up a chain of turns for a big follower burst is a fun combo moment.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A visible round-end steal that can swing a contest; fine, can be planned around.

name: Bodyguards
why: Quiet steal immunity; fine.

name: Tryout
why: Using a shop member's On Recruit without buying it is a clever, fun moment.

name: Night Owls
why: A free extra minion each round from II is a strong, fun boost.

name: Housewarming
why: A free member of a new color is a satisfying gain.
